fields: Do Not Start With This When

rows.Main Input: spatial expression matrix + spatial coordinates + cell type composition or labels
rows.Key Difference: Focuses on cell type-specific spatial variation with a spatially varying coefficient formulation rather than a broader unified or conditional-correlation test.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed confirms PMID 39865128 and DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-56280-4; the frozen registry provides the GitHub link. Layer 2 synthesis: comparator placement and resource uncertainty; the 2026 ctSVG benchmark reports strong predictive performance but possible spurious signals from non-target cell types.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the question is explicitly cell type-specific SVG detection and strong predictive sensitivity across spatial patterns is desired.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When cell type composition is unavailable, unreliable, or the analysis must minimize spurious signals from non-target cell types.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Cell type deconvolution or label error can propagate into ctSVG calls; benchmark evidence flags possible non-target-cell signal leakage.

rows.Main Input: spatial expression matrix + spatial coordinates + cell type composition or labels
rows.Main Output: cell-type-specific SVG calls and significance statistics
rows.Key Difference: Targets the cell type-specific SVG question directly and is benchmark-screened as relatively stronger for false-positive control than some sensitivity-oriented alternatives.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed confirms PMID 41361894 and DOI 10.1186/s13059-025-03870-6. Layer 2 synthesis: no primary code link was present in the frozen input or PubMed metadata; the 2026 ctSVG benchmark supports branch-local false-positive-control caveats, not runtime readiness.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the cell type-specific branch needs conservative false-positive control and the method-paper assumptions match the data.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When an immediately traceable code source is required for engineering audit or when cell type estimates are weak.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: False-positive control can trade off against sensitivity; cell type composition uncertainty remains a branch-level confounder.

rows.Main Input: spatial expression matrix + spatial coordinates + cell type composition or labels
rows.Main Use in This Topic: cell-type-specific SVG detection with unified modeling
rows.Key Difference: Uses a unified statistical framework for ctSVG detection rather than a narrower coefficient or conditional-correlation formulation.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed confirms PMID 39979358 and DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-57117-w; the frozen registry provides the GitHub link. Layer 2 synthesis: branch positioning uses the unified-model claim and the 2026 ctSVG benchmark, which supports local performance guidance but not a global ranking.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the task is ctSVG detection and a unified statistical-model framing is preferred for multiple cell-type spatial patterns.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the analysis lacks credible cell type context or needs the most conservative false-positive-control route first.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Performance depends on cell type context quality; benchmark support is branch-local and dataset-dependent.

rows.Main Input: spatial expression matrix + spatial coordinates, typically tissue-scale tumor spatial data
rows.Main Use in This Topic: gene-centric tissue-pattern mining rather than classical hypothesis-test SVG calling
rows.Main Output: gene-level spatial tissue patterns and interpretable pattern summaries
rows.Key Difference: Prioritizes gene-centric tissue-pattern interpretation, especially in tumor contexts, instead of only returning a ranked SVG list.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed confirms PMID 39947134 and DOI 10.1016/j.xgen.2025.100771; the frozen registry provides the GitHub link. Layer 2 synthesis: this is retained as a boundary branch because its main role is pattern mining, not standard SVG hypothesis testing.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the goal is gene-centric spatial tissue-pattern interpretation, especially in tumor tissue, rather than a generic SVG screen.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the deliverable must be a conventional calibrated SVG p-value/ranking workflow.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Tumor-pattern interpretability can be context-specific; benchmark evidence does not establish general SVG-detection superiority.

rows.Main Use in This Topic: overall SVG detection with dimension-agnostic granularity testing
rows.Key Difference: Uses a granularity-based non-parametric statistic rather than Gaussian-process, kernel, or nearest-neighbor Gaussian-process modeling.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed confirms PMID 37963892 and DOI 10.1038/s41467-023-43256-5; the frozen registry provides the GitHub link. Layer 2 synthesis: closest alternatives and resource labels are conservative because retrieved benchmarks do not settle BSP as a universal first choice.
rows.Best First Choice When: When a dimension-agnostic, non-parametric overall SVG test is desired for heterogeneous spatial structures.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When branch-specific benchmark guidance favors SPARK-X/nnSVG or when cell type-specific SVGs are the central question.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Granularity choices and heterogeneous pattern scales can affect interpretation; independent branch-local benchmark support is limited in this package.

rows.Main Input: large-scale spatial expression matrix + spatial coordinates
rows.Main Use in This Topic: fast overall SVG detection for large-scale spatial transcriptomics
rows.Key Difference: Frames SVG detection as a fast distribution-free test for large-scale data rather than a model-heavy spatial process fit.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed confirms PMID 38972896 and DOI 10.1038/s41467-024-49846-1; the title directly supports a large-scale/fast claim. Layer 2 synthesis: no primary code link was present in the frozen input or PubMed metadata, and scale support is not a BioHarness runtime claim.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the overall SVG problem is large-scale and a distribution-free statistical test is scientifically appropriate.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When traceable code access is required before method consideration or when cell type-specific SVGs are needed.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Large-scale speed claims come from method-paper evidence; calibration and cross-method behavior should be checked locally.

rows.Main Use in This Topic: scalable overall SVG detection with nearest-neighbor Gaussian-process approximation
rows.Key Difference: Keeps the Gaussian-process SVG framing while using nearest-neighbor approximation for improved scalability.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed confirms PMID 37429865 and DOI 10.1038/s41467-023-39748-z; the frozen registry provides the GitHub link. Layer 2 synthesis: benchmark-screening supports inclusion in the overall SVG benchmark branch, but ranking remains branch-local.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the user wants a Gaussian-process-style overall SVG method but SpatialDE-like scaling is a concern.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When cell type-specific SVGs, cell-type-conditional correlations, or gene-centric tissue-pattern mining are the actual task.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Nearest-neighbor approximations may change sensitivity to broad versus local spatial patterns; calibration should be read with benchmark caveats.

rows.Main Use in This Topic: overall SVG detection after self-organizing-map compression
rows.Key Difference: Uses self-organizing-map representation to reduce spatial complexity before SVG testing.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed confirms PMID 34165490 and DOI 10.1093/bioinformatics/btab471; the frozen registry provides the GitHub link. Layer 2 synthesis: scalability and comparator placement are conservative because benchmark conclusions are not converted into universal ordering.
rows.Best First Choice When: When self-organizing-map summarization is attractive for an overall SVG screen on spatially structured data.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the main selection criterion is branch-specific benchmark performance or cell type-resolved interpretation.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Spatial compression can obscure fine-grained patterns; public evidence is not sufficient here to make dataset-general calibration claims.

rows.Main Use in This Topic: overall SVG detection with count-aware spatial modeling
rows.Main Output: ranked SVGs and calibrated test statistics when assumptions hold
rows.Key Difference: Uses a generalized linear spatial model for counts, making it more count-aware than earlier Gaussian-process-only baselines but less scalable than SPARK-X.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed confirms PMID 31988518 and DOI 10.1038/s41592-019-0701-7; the frozen registry provides the GitHub link. Layer 2 synthesis: benchmark-screening supports SPARK as a key comparator, while later scalable branches may be preferred for large data.
rows.Best First Choice When: When count-aware overall SVG modeling is desired and data size is moderate enough for model-based testing.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the main concern is very large-scale throughput, where SPARK-X or other scalable methods should be read first.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Model calibration and runtime can vary across data technologies; benchmark evidence should be used branch-locally.

rows.Main Input: large spatial expression matrix + spatial coordinates
rows.Main Use in This Topic: scalable and robust overall SVG detection
rows.Key Difference: Replaces SPARK-style model fitting with a scalable non-parametric covariance test for large spatial datasets.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed confirms PMID 34154649 and DOI 10.1186/s13059-021-02404-0; the frozen registry provides the code link. Layer 2 synthesis: the 2025 broad benchmark reports SPARK-X as strong overall, but this supports only the overall-SVG branch rather than a global default.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the task is overall SVG detection on large data and branch-local benchmark evidence is allowed to guide a scalable first read.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When cell type-specific, conditional-on-cell-type, or gene-centric tissue-pattern interpretation is the target.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Strong benchmark performance does not remove dataset-specific calibration checks or make this a universal default.

rows.Main Output: ranked SVGs and spatial expression pattern statistics
rows.Key Difference: Provides the canonical Gaussian-process SVG formulation, useful as a conceptual baseline even when newer scalable methods are preferred.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed confirms PMID 29553579 and DOI 10.1038/nmeth.4636; the frozen registry provides the GitHub link. Layer 2 synthesis: treated as a canonical baseline, but broad benchmark literature motivates caution on scale and calibration.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the user needs a canonical, interpretable Gaussian-process SVG baseline for modest-sized data or literature comparability.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When large-scale throughput, branch-local benchmark performance, or cell type-specific inference is the main requirement.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Canonical status can encourage overuse; scaling and calibration limitations should be checked before interpreting rankings.

rows.Main Input: spatial expression matrix + spatial coordinates, with cell-type-aware interpretation when applicable
rows.Main Use in This Topic: detection and interpretation of spatial gene expression variation
rows.Main Output: spatial variation coefficients and gene-level variation evidence
rows.Key Difference: Emphasizes interpretable spatial variation coefficients rather than only binary/ranked SVG calls.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed confirms PMID 38641849 and DOI 10.1186/s13059-024-03245-3. Layer 2 synthesis: code access remains unclear from the frozen input and PubMed metadata; the 2026 ctSVG benchmark mentions spVC in the cell-type-specific benchmark context, but the registry places this row in the overall branch.
rows.Best First Choice When: When interpretation of spatial variation magnitude is more important than a conventional SVG ranking alone.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the task requires an immediately traceable implementation link or a strictly branch-pure overall SVG test.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: The method sits near the boundary between overall and cell-type-aware interpretation; use care when comparing it to branch-pure methods.

rows.Main Input: spatial expression matrix + spatial coordinates + cell type landscape
rows.Main Use in This Topic: finding spatially correlated genes conditional on cell type landscape
rows.Key Difference: Conditions spatial gene-correlation discovery on the cell type landscape rather than directly calling cell type-specific SVGs.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed confirms PMID 40275395 and DOI 10.1186/s13059-025-03554-1. Layer 2 synthesis: treated as a conditional-correlation branch; no primary code link was present in frozen input or PubMed metadata.
rows.Best First Choice When: When the scientific question is spatial correlation among genes after conditioning on the cell type landscape.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the requested output is standard overall SVG ranking or direct ctSVG calls by cell type.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Conditioning can remove or preserve signals depending on cell type landscape quality; interpretation should not be collapsed into overall SVG ranking.

rows.Main Input: spatial expression matrix + spatial coordinates + cell type effect estimates
rows.Main Use in This Topic: SVG clustering adjusted for cell type effect and downstream domain-supporting feature selection
rows.Main Output: cell-type-adjusted SVG clusters / selected spatial features
rows.Key Difference: Clusters SVGs while adjusting for cell type effects, placing it between SVG detection, feature selection, and domain-support workflows.
rows.Evidence Note: Direct evidence: PubMed confirms PMID 40985765 and DOI 10.1093/nar/gkaf936; PubMed title uses SPACE, while the registry label SPACE-SVG disambiguates it. Layer 2 synthesis: this is a boundary row because its output supports SVG clustering and spatial-domain detection rather than only standalone SVG testing.
rows.Best First Choice When: When SVG grouping after cell type-effect adjustment is needed for feature selection or domain-oriented interpretation.
rows.Do Not Start With This When: When the task is a simple overall SVG p-value/ranking or when no cell type-effect adjustment should enter the analysis.
rows.Signal-risk Caveat: Boundary with domain detection and feature selection is real; cell type-effect adjustment can change which genes appear spatially variable.
